# TV desktop

The TV desktop is a hidden second monitor that gets cast instead of the laptop
screen. You arrange it with Omarchy's own window management; the laptop stays
private. Everything is driven by `raytube-tv` (Python, repo root); run it with no
arguments for the full command list (`up`, `down`, `send`, `to-tv`, `back`, `home`,
`scene`, `next`, `prev`, `layout`, `swap`, `rotate`, `rotate-scene`, `board`, `browser`,
`video-full`, `native`, `pull`, `tv-mode`, `key`, `status`, `json`). `sync-mode` is a
leftover of the removed arrow sync mode: its `raytube-sync` submap is no longer defined.

## The TV output

- `raytube-tv up [WxH]` creates a headless Hyprland output named **`TV`**
  (`hyprctl output create headless TV`), sizes it with
  `hl.monitor({ output = "TV", mode = "WxH@30", position = "auto-center-up" })`
  (the TV sits **above** the laptop, centred, so the mouse goes straight up into it;
  `auto-center-down` instead when `~/.local/state/display-flip` is `2`, the bed mount),
  shows the first scene, and loads a PipeWire null sink **`raytube_tv`**
  ("TV"). Chromecast casts use 1920x1080; an Apple TV uses its chosen picture size
  (`raytube-cast size`, default 1920x1080; 720p / 1080p / 1440p).
- A persistent rule in `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` keeps `TV` at its size, 30 Hz,
  above the laptop (below when flipped) across `hyprctl reload`. The size comes from
  `~/.local/state/raytube/tv-size`, written by `raytube-tv up`. A fixed 1920x1080
  there shrank a 2560x1440 Apple TV cast on reload (2026-09-26).
- **The top bar appears on `TV`** (the active bar is Omarchy's built-in `omarchy.bar`,
  drawn on every monitor; the clone `nathank.bar` that skipped `TV` is disabled because
  cloned bars get no plugin services, which blanked bar widgets). Planned, not built (T-24):
  make `TV` one bar-height taller and cast only the area below the bar
  (`wf-recorder -o TV -g "X,Y+22 WxH"`; `-o` is required, since `-g` alone matches the
  laptop output), plus a workspace rule for `tv-*` (`gaps_out = 0, gaps_in = 0,
  border_size = 0, decorate = false`). Both were proven by hand; neither is in the
  scripts or `~/.config/hypr` yet.
- `raytube-tv down` stops rotation, **closes** the board and TV browser,
  brings every other window home to the laptop's current workspace (audio
  routed back), removes the output and unloads the sink.
- `raytube-cast` handles this: desktop mode runs `up` before the cast, captures
  only `-o TV` and records audio from `raytube_tv.monitor`; `stop` runs `down`;
  `release` ends the cast but keeps the TV desktop.
- The Display menu hides `TV` from its DISPLAYS list.

## Sending windows

- `raytube-tv to-tv` (⌘⌃↑, TV mode S): the focused window goes to the TV's current
  scene and its audio streams move to `raytube_tv`. Sent windows are pushed onto a
  stack. `send` does the same but toggles: on a window already on the TV it comes home.
- `raytube-tv home` (⌘⌃↓, TV mode B): brings the focused window home if it is on the TV,
  else the most recently sent one (`back`), so it needs no focus on the TV. (Focus
  follows the mouse: with the old ⌃⌥Tab + ⌘⌥⇧T keys, the window under the pointer was
  sent instead.)
- Audio follows by process id (`application.process.id` of sink inputs), so
  sending one Firefox window moves all of that Firefox's audio.

## Scenes

A scene is a Hyprland workspace on `TV` named `tv-<id>`, listed in
`~/.config/raytube/tv.json` (defaults: `main` 120 s, `board` 120 s, `watch` 300 s; all
three are at 15 s for testing until T-3 restores `tv.json.before-test`). Moves to a
scene use `workspace = "name:tv-<id>"` (without `name:` a move to a workspace
that doesn't exist yet silently fails).

- `scene <id>`, `next` / `prev` (TV mode N / P): step through scenes with windows,
  without taking focus from the laptop.
- `json`: full state for the Display menu (scenes, window counts, current,
  layout, rotation, seconds to next).

## Layouts

`layout full|split|pip` arranges the current scene; `layout next` (TV mode L) steps
through the L cycle below; `swap` (TV mode M) swaps the main window with the inset. The main window is remembered per scene
(largest window by default).

| Layout | How |
|---|---|
| full | main `fullscreen_state({ internal = 2 })` (true fullscreen: no gaps or border) |
| split | everything tiled side by side (50/50) |
| pip | main `fullscreen_state({ internal = 1 })` (maximized) + others floating at 30% size in the bottom-right corner, **not pinned** |

Lua dispatcher notes (Hyprland 0.56 Lua config, via `hyprctl eval
'hl.dispatch(...)'`): `fullscreen_state({ internal = 0, client = 0 })` clears
fullscreen; floating windows stay above a maximized window; `move({ x, y })`
uses global layout coordinates, so add the TV output's `x`/`y`; pinned windows
follow every workspace on a monitor (bad for rotation).


**L cycle** (`layout next` via `layout_steps()`, 2026-09-26, the user's order): each window
as the PiP main (most recently sent first), then split, then each window full screen, so
two windows give five steps; one window only has full. Two-window split
is forced side by side (dwindle stacks them on first split; `side_by_side()` flips it
with `togglesplit`, then hands focus back). **Sending** a window to the TV makes it the
scene's main window, and a `full` scene with other windows becomes `pip`, so a window sent
over a full-screen video shows up with the video in the corner instead of behind it.
## Rotation

`rotate on|off|toggle` (TV mode R) runs the systemd user unit `raytube-rotation`
(`raytube-tv rotate-daemon`): it shows each scene that has windows and
`rotate: true`, for that scene's `seconds`. `rotate-scene <id> on|off` edits
membership. The menu shows a countdown.

## Family board

`raytube-tv board` opens `board/index.html` in a dedicated Chromium `--app`
window (profile `~/.local/share/raytube/board-chromium`, audio to the TV
sink) and places it in the `board` scene. Chromium ignores `--class` in
`--app` mode: the window class is URL-based
(`chrome-__home_nathank_workspace_raytube_board_index.html-Default`), matched by
`is_board()`.

The page is drawn for 1920x1080: live clock, weather line, one column per
person (Alex, Sam, Kai 10, Mia 5 with big words and stars) and a three.js
particle glow (vendored `board/vendor/three.min.js`, r128) capped at 30 fps at
DPR 1. Content comes from `board/data.js` (mock data), reloaded every minute.
Cost while visible: about 16% of one core.


**Calendar panel** (added 2026-09-26, Kai's idea): right-hand column, 27vw wide. It shows
the weekday and "Day N of 7", a Mon–Sun strip (gone days filled, today lit), the current
month Monday-first (today circled, this week shaded, up to four dots per day in the family
colours, amber for `family`), and "Coming up": today plus the next days with events, capped
at about six events so it fits at 1080p. Events are in `board/data.js` under
`calendar.events`: `{ day: <days from today> | date: "YYYY-MM-DD", time, title, who }`.
The sample uses relative days so it always looks current. Preview without the TV:
`chromium --headless=new --window-size=1920,1080 --screenshot=… file://…/board/index.html`
(set `TZ` for the right clock).
## TV browser and native YouTube

- `raytube-tv browser [url]`: a separate kiosk Firefox (`--no-remote`, profile
  `~/.local/share/raytube/tv-firefox`, `--kiosk`, `--remote-debugging-port
  9337`) with `MOZ_DRM_DEVICE=/dev/dri/renderD129` and `PULSE_SINK=raytube_tv`.
  Its `user.js` enables VA-API and disables VP9/AV1 so YouTube serves H.264,
  decoded on the Intel GPU (verified: `i965_drv_video.so` in its RDD process).
  Opens in the `watch` scene. It is signed out of YouTube (own profile). Using the
  everyday profile instead is planned (T-27) but not built; remote control on the
  everyday Firefox (`--remote-debugging-port`) was tried and removed (striped URL bar,
  `navigator.webdriver = true` on every site).
- **Decode caveat (2026-09-27):** a YouTube livestream replay was seen decoding in
  **software** (`av:h264` threads, ~56% of a core) despite the hardware-decode setup.
  Cause not known yet.
- `raytube-media.py` (run via `uv run --with pychromecast --with websockets`)
  talks WebDriver BiDi to that browser (`tv-video`, `tv-pause`, `tv-open`,
  `tv-fullscreen`) and
  pychromecast to the Chromecast (`cc-status`, `cc-youtube`, `cc-quit`).
- `raytube-tv native` (TV mode Y): reads the video id and position, pauses the TV
  browser, `raytube-cast release` (ends the cast, keeps the TV desktop), plays
  it in the Chromecast's own YouTube app from the same spot, writes
  `native.json`. Pressing again runs `pull`.
- `raytube-tv pull`: asks the Chromecast what its YouTube app plays and where,
  quits the app, restarts the TV-desktop cast and opens the video at that
  position in the TV browser, full screen in the Watch scene. T-25 plans the
  picture-in-picture version (TV mode V).

Native YouTube and pull are **not yet tested on the Chromecast** (T-2).

## Hotkeys

In `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua`. Redesigned 2026-09-26 after the nine ⌘⌥ combos
proved too hard to remember: two arrows for the everyday move, one combo for the rest.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘⌃↑ (Command+Ctrl+Up) | send the focused window to the TV (`raytube-tv to-tv`) |
| ⌘⌃↓ (Command+Ctrl+Down) | bring the focused TV window home, else the last one sent (`raytube-tv home`) |
| ⌘⇧T (Command+Shift+T) | **TV mode**: a cheat-sheet notification, then one letter |

TV mode is the Hyprland submap `raytube-tv` (`raytube-tv tv-mode`). Each key runs
`raytube-tv key <letter>`, which leaves TV mode first, so a letter never lands in an
app. Any other key (a `catchall` bind) also just leaves TV mode.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| S | send this window to the TV |
| B | bring a window back |
| N / P | next / previous scene |
| L | next layout, in this order: PiP (newest-sent window big) → PiP reversed → side by side → full (one) → full (the other) |
| M | make the other window the main one (`swap`) |
| F | full screen the video: TV browser becomes main, layout full, then YouTube's own player goes full screen (`video-full` → `raytube-media.py tv-fullscreen`) |
| R | rotation on/off |
| Y | native YouTube on the Chromecast / back |
| O | on/off: start or stop casting (`raytube-cast tv`, last receiver) |
| A | **re-sync** sound and picture: restarts the cast session (`raytube-cast resync`) |
| Esc | leave TV mode |

The letters live in `KEYS` in `raytube-tv`; the submap's key list in
`bindings.lua` must match. Hotkeys run with `RAYTUBE_NOTIFY=1` for a brief
notification.

**Test gotcha:** focus follows the mouse, so a scripted `to-tv` sends whatever window
is under the pointer. Focus the target window explicitly before each call (a test
did this to a private window on 2026-09-26).

## Display menu (nathank.monitor)

**Cast menu plugin (2026-09-27):** the cast and TV-desktop controls below now also ship as a
standalone Omarchy plugin, `nathank.raytube` (repo `../omarchy-raytube`, MIT; installed here with
`omarchy plugin add file://…`). It shows "raytube tools not installed" when `raytube-cast` isn't on
PATH and "Looking for TVs…" while discovering. The Display-panel clone below still carries the same
controls on this machine until the author retires it (two cast icons in the bar meanwhile).


CAST section: **Screen | TV desktop** chips (switching mid-cast restarts the
cast in the new mode), receiver list with casting state. TV DESKTOP section
(only while `TV` exists): Full / Split / PiP / rotation, Board / Browser /
YouTube ⇄ TV app buttons, scene rows (click to show, ↻ toggles rotation). While casting to an
Apple TV the CAST section also shows **Sound sync − / +** (live, 50 ms steps), **720p | 1080p |
1440p** (picture size, restarts the cast) and **Re-sync TV**.
